s1.syndrome_frame: Painful swelling and ulceration of the glans penis with systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Painful swelling and ulceration of the glans penis
Grossly edematous glans penis and corona
Tender, firm ulcer on the ventral surface of the penis with overlying black eschar and granulation tissue
Dermal infiltrate of atypical lymphocytes on biopsy
key_facts: 78-year-old man presented with painful swelling and ulceration of the glans penis
Symptoms duration of 1 month
Previous medical history of elevated white blood cell count and inguinal lymphadenopathy
Previous treatments with topical antibiotics, antifungal agents, and cephalexin showed no improvement
Routine blood test results were within normal limits
Cultures, assays, and blood tests evaluating for viral, bacterial, or fungal etiology were negative
Biopsy of the glans penis ulcer showed dermal infiltrate of atypical lymphocytes
PCR analysis revealed a clonal IgH gene rearrangement
PET-CT scan demonstrated FDG-avid abdominal and peripancreatic lymph nodes

shortlist.label: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of atypical lymphocytes, clonal IgH gene rearrangement, and FDG-avid lymph nodes

shortlist.label: Primary cutaneous follicle center lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Dermal infiltrate of atypical lymphocytes and presence of CD20+, CD79a+, and CD5+ cells

shortlist.label: Primary cutaneous marginal zone lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Ulceration and swelling of the glans penis with negative cultures and assays for viral, bacterial, or fungal etiology

shortlist.label: Mantle cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Systemic symptoms and presence of atypical lymphocytes with clonal IgH gene rearrangement

shortlist.label: Follicular lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of atypical lymphocytes and clonal IgH gene rearrangement with FDG-avid lymph nodes

raw.rationale: The presence of a dermal infiltrate of atypical lymphocytes that are CD20+, CD79a+, and CD5+, along with a clonal IgH gene rearrangement and FDG-avid lymph nodes on PET-CT scan, supports the diagnosis of Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, which is a common and aggressive type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma.

rejected.label: Primary cutaneous follicle center lymphoma
rejected.why: This type of lymphoma typically has a more indolent course and is less likely to present with systemic symptoms or aggressive features.

rejected.label: Primary cutaneous marginal zone lymphoma
rejected.why: This type of lymphoma is often associated with chronic inflammation or infection and is less likely to have a clonal IgH gene rearrangement or systemic involvement.

rejected.label: Mantle cell lymphoma
rejected.why: This type of lymphoma typically has a distinct immunophenotypic profile, including CD5+ and CD23-, and is less likely to present with a solitary cutaneous lesion.

rejected.label: Follicular lymphoma
rejected.why: This type of lymphoma is often associated with a more indolent course and is less likely to present with aggressive features or a solitary cutaneous lesion.
